name: Pumble
tagline: Run straightforward team channels, direct messages, threads, and file sharing

pricing.notes: Official Pro monthly seat price with annual billing.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited users, message history and channels; 10 GB storage/workspace; 1:1 meetings; 3 third-party integrations plus Clockify and Plaky

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 10 GB storage/paid seat; 10 integrations; group meetings

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 20 GB storage/paid seat; unlimited integrations; meeting recording; 5 free single-channel guests per paid seat

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 100 GB storage/paid seat; SSO and retention controls

tiers.name: CAKE.com Bundle
tiers.limits: Pumble plus Clockify and Plaky; charged once per unique user across the bundled products

pricing.freeTierCaps: unlimited users, messages and channels; 10 GB/workspace; 1:1 meetings; 3 external integrations plus Clockify and Plaky
pricing.hiddenCosts: Owners, admins, members and multi-channel guests count as paid seats; deactivated users do not. Business includes 5 free single-channel guests per paid seat, but multi-channel guests are paid. Bundle billing counts each unique user across the included apps.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Pumble, run straightforward team channels, direct messages, threads, and file sharing. The hard boundary is cross-platform apps, push, guest access, admin controls, and hosted reliability, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a private team space with channels, direct messages, threads, and file sharing, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: cross-platform apps, push, guest access, admin controls, and hosted reliability
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pumble because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Chanty Free
alternatives.desc: Five people get unlimited history, files, tasks and one-to-one calls; the sixth human triggers billing.

facts.install: Hosted signup; use Chanty's web, desktop, or mobile clients
facts.dataFormat: Chats, task records, users, and files live in Chanty's cloud; workspace data export is a Business-plan feature rather than part of the free plan.
facts.gapVsPaid: Chanty Free includes unlimited history, files, tasks, and one-to-one calls, but it stops at five members and free workspaces cannot export their data.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no technical setup blocker, but the free workspace is limited to five members, so the sixth teammate forces a migration or payment.

alternatives.name: Element
alternatives.desc: Free Matrix chat with rooms, threads, files and proper apps; familiar enough after the first vocabulary lesson.

facts.install: Use a free Matrix account in Element Web/mobile/desktop, or deploy Element Server Suite on your own infrastructure
facts.dataFormat: Rooms, event history, account data, and media live on the selected Matrix homeserver; encrypted-room keys remain on clients and can be backed up through Matrix's key-backup system.
facts.gapVsPaid: Element supplies rooms, threads, files, and apps, but the Matrix homeserver model and vocabulary are less straightforward for a team expecting Pumble's Slack-like conventions.
facts.setupBlocker: The clean hosted path is easy, but self-hosting the current Element Server Suite means operating a Matrix homeserver and its Kubernetes/Helm-based stack.

alternatives.name: Mattermost Team Edition
alternatives.desc: Full self-hosted team chat for under 250 users; free software, non-free evenings.

facts.install: Install the official Linux binary with PostgreSQL, then configure systemd, TLS/reverse proxy, SMTP, and file storage
facts.dataFormat: Channels, posts, users, and configuration live in PostgreSQL; file attachments live in the Mattermost data directory or configured S3-compatible object storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mattermost Team Edition is a fuller self-hosted chat, but PostgreSQL, TLS, SMTP, storage, backups, upgrades, and uptime become the team's responsibility.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real Linux service deployment, PostgreSQL, SMTP, DNS/TLS, storage, backups, and upgrades, not an app-store install.

alternatives.name: Pumble Free
alternatives.desc: The same product keeps unlimited users, channels and history; storage, calls and integrations are where the invoice waits.

facts.install: Hosted signup; use the browser or Pumble's desktop/mobile apps
facts.dataFormat: Messages, channels, user records, and files live in Pumble's cloud; workspace owners can export public-channel data as a ZIP with message data and file links.
facts.gapVsPaid: Pumble Free keeps unlimited users, channels, and history, but free group calls and screen sharing are absent and storage and integration allowances are much tighter.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no installation hurdle, but migration still requires inviting everyone and rebuilding channels and integrations; free exports exclude private channels and direct messages.

alternatives.name: Rocket.Chat Community
alternatives.desc: Slack-shaped chat for up to a hundred concurrent users; MongoDB and upgrades are now yours.

facts.install: Deploy the Community workspace with Docker Compose, Podman, or Kubernetes
facts.dataFormat: Users, rooms, messages, and most metadata live in MongoDB; uploads live on local storage or a configured object-storage backend.
facts.gapVsPaid: Rocket.Chat Community is capable and self-hosted, but MongoDB administration, upgrades, and its 100-concurrent-user Community limit are more burdensome than Pumble.
facts.setupBlocker: A production installation requires MongoDB, DNS/TLS, email, backups, upgrades, and enough capacity planning to stay within the Community plan's 100-concurrent-user limit.

alternatives.name: Zulip
alternatives.desc: Channels become streams and every conversation gets a topic; async teams usually call that an upgrade.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Pumble in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a private team space with channels, direct messages, threads, and file sharing, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
